script.text: Meta's AI bill could reach 145 billion dollars. Did that sink the Nasdaq?

The Nasdaq fell more than 2 percent on Thursday, Reuters reports. Its chip index had the biggest drop since July, as Lam Research shares plunged 10 percent after its results. Yahoo Finance says Meta shares fell nearly 7 percent after the company's earnings.

Meta now expects 2026 capital spending of 135 to 145 billion dollars, according to Bloomberg. It also created a new class of non-voting shares, which it could use to help fund its AI buildout. Meta says Mark Zuckerberg keeps control.

Reuters says the steep bill for AI buildouts punished other tech favorites too. Yahoo Finance reports oil at a five-month high sent investors toward bonds, and Treasury yields fell. The Dow was little changed.
Will investors keep worrying about AI spending next week? Yes or no?
